name: Daybreak Organic Coffee
description: Complex with a Smooth Finish.

rating.description: Really good, I enjoy it a lot. Dark roast, whole bean, not that different than their regular dark roast. It is complex and very smooth.

name: Hair of the Goat
description: On paper, Hair of the Goat should taste enormously complex with a host of competing flavors; in reality, the blend of two distinct Latin single-origins and one Indonesian ends up as the best introduction to our coffees and one of our most drinkable brews. From a palette standpoint, it offers a little bit of everything, and when customers ask for either a house- or breakfast-blend, we suggest Hair of the Goat.

rating.description: It has a tiny bit of bitterness, in a good way. Smooth, drink it black.

name: Santa's Private Reserve 2024
description: A collaboration with Portland Coffee Roasters. This festive brew captures the festive spirit in every sip.

rating.description: A really nice coffee stout. Slightly bitter, I definitely get the stout taste, and I definitely get the coffee taste. I will have this again.

name: Oktommegang
description: Join us in celebrating the world's favorite beer festival with Oktommegang, our take on the classic Marzen-style Lager! Pouring with a rich amber hue and topped with a foamy white cap, it's the perfect brew to fill your stein and set the table for an authentic European experience. Brewed with pristine water from Ommegang's aquifer, Oktommegang boasts notes of bready caramel malts balanced by a hint of noble hops. Simple, clean, and easy to enjoy, we invite you to savor this generous yet drinkable fall favorite. Prost!

rating.description: It's also part of the OMG series. And it is generous yet drinkable!

name: High Desert Sunrise
description: Characterized by sparkling citrus, honey and candied hazelnut, this blend consists of Latin American coffees. The roast level is on the lighter side, highlighting the bright acidity and sweetness of these coffees. The perfect coffee for crisp summer mornings in the Central Oregon High Desert.

rating.description: I like this. I'll go with their claims bright acidity. It's very easy to make without any bitterness.

name: Eleven of Spades
description: Our house blend, silky smooth chocolate throughout, sweet dark fruit tones and a lingering German chocolate finish. Eleven of Spades cuts through milk like a knife and stands on its own deliciously.

rating.description: Not bad, a little bitter for my taste. I definitely taste some of the chocolate notes they’re talking about, but it’s slightly bitterer than most of the coffees I drink.

name: Let the Games Begin
description: Waking up early to catch all the action from France? Count us in! This Trade-exclusive blend, inspired (and created) by pro athletes, unites coffees from around the world (Colombia and Tanzania) for an energizing blend that makes any early-rising spectator feel like a winner.

rating.description: A medium roast. That’s all it says. WHAT IS IN YOUR COFFEE, PEOPLE?!? It’s not my favorite. I don’t think I would buy this coffee again from Trade, just because I’ve had so many good ones from them.

name: Oktober Fest-Märzen
description: Rich, amber-golden color. Deep, inviting, malty nose and bready, wonderful flavor that’s an ode to barley. Medium to big body, with a touch of warming alcohol on the finish. Soft dryness from long maturation.

rating.description: It’s got a very nice multi-flavor dark color, it’s a tiny touch flat compared to other beers I’ve had recently, but the flavor more than makes up for it. It goes down smooth, it’s definitely thumbs up, would recommend, no desperation needed.

name: Decaf Fool's Gold
description: Decaf Fool’s Gold is for those that love coffee, but prefer to avoid the caffeine. Featuring two coffees selected for their smooth and nutty taste, we assure you will not find a better decaf anywhere else.

rating.description: Little lighter than I would normally take it. Not something I would drink straight, but I added a little bit of cream and now it’s quite pleasant. Would I recommend it? Yes, I like it.

name: Guatemala
description: We’ve had this Guatemala since we started way back in 2009. It’s a flagship amazing coffee and essentially defines Trailhead. With notes of Cacao, Almond and Pecan this coffee is your reliable, comfortable friend. It’s an honor for us to carry you from sleepy to full consciousness so you can crush your day. Getting this right with a lovely experience as you are sipping and also how it impacts your body and mind. I very much need my coffee to be amazing to gather enough stoke to make the day count. I always reach for Trailhead and often the choice is Guatemala to make this happen.

rating.description: What do I taste? I probably taste the almond and the pecan more than the Cacau. If I do taste chocolate, it’s definitely bitter chocolate, which is fine. I have no problem with that. Bitter chocolate is good for a lot of things. I do recommend.

name: Nightcap Noir Decaf
description: Making decaf actually dark and roasty while preserving flavor is even harder than with caffeinated coffee; Joe does a great job here with syrupy dark chocolate notes enveloping all that roast.

rating.description: It's a dark roast decaf, and it is really yummy!

name: Colombia Nariño
description: DOMA's current Colombian offering comes from the great coffee-growing region of Nariño, and brings some lovely citrus acidity and brown sugar sweetness.

rating.description: I've got that Doma aroma going. I definitely taste the lemoniness. It's super mild. I like it.

name: Decaf Colombia Amigos Del Huila
description: This sugarcane process decaffeinated community lot reminds of of honey, brown sugar and cherry.

rating.description: It's says it's comforting, and dammit, I feel comforted right now!

name: SELECT Coffee Whole Bean Dark Roast Italian Roast
description: Tasting Notes: Hearty, smoky, chocolate. Our Signature Select Italian roast begins with a blend of Latin American beans that are sturdy enough to handle the extreme dark roasting style that originated in southern Italy. This longer and deeper roasting style mellows acidity, deepens body and sweetness, and adds smokiness and flavors of dark chocolate to the coffee. Enjoy this boldly roasted coffee, with its creamy body and hearty finish.

rating.description: Part of my special Peter's blend mix of coffees!

name: Odin
description: Tamper provides ZERO description of this coffee, or anything else.

rating.description: Part of my special Peter's blend mix of coffees!

name: Màkku Blueberry
description: If you love the idea of a boozy, bubbly, blueberry frozen yogurt, this one’s for you! A hint sweet. Aspartame-Free.

rating.description: It's like an alcoholic yogurt, and I don't think that's a good thing. If someone was going to shoot my family if I didn't drink this, I'd drink it. If they were going to shoot me if I didn't drink this, I'd say please shoot me.

name: Decaf Colombia Palo Rosa
description: We have never been happier with the flavor profile of any other decaffeination process that we have tried. We roast this coffee to a medium roast in order to create an accessible every day coffee that tastes delicious with or without cream or sugar.

rating.description: I gotta say, I'm liking this. I think I would prefer a darker roast, but this is very drinkable. This might be an enthusiastic thumbs-up. Like, I would not have to be desperate to drink this.

name: Alma Coffee Honey Process
description: Today, our honey and natural processing story has made leaps and bounds from its genesis. With new processing facilities and dry milling equipment to ensure consistent quality, we have perfected our practices taste the improvement each and every coffee harvest. Honey-Drizzled Mango, Cherry, Grilled Pineapple.

rating.description: We definitely tasted the pineapple. The rest of the flavors are quite subtle, but it's a good, even cup of coffee and I'll drink it again.

name: Slumber Decaf
description: Slumber is our second decaf offering here at Alma. We wanted to round out our options for decaf lovers and include something a little lighter than our original decaf roast, Dreamer. For Slumber, we absolutely love the surprising complexity that you’ll get out of this roast and truly think you’ll be surprised to learn decaf offerings could be so delicious. Notes: Almond, Chocolate, Sweet Pastry.

rating.description: I would not call it sweet. I do taste the chocolate and maybe the almond. It's good. I will drink this decaf again. I like it, I recommend it, I will thumbs it up the ying yang.

name: Organic Funky Chicken Medium Dark Roast Signature Blend Coffee
description: Our Go-To Crowd-Pleaser Coffee. When we first began roasting coffee we wanted to create a blend that would appeal to all audiences. With a lot of practice and a little luck, we created a winner. This blend features three coffees from three origins, roasted to three different profiles to create one of the most complex yet approachable medium to dark roast blends you can find. Tasting notes: Dark Chocolate Torte, Praline, Citrus, Nutty.

rating.description: It's ok. I would thumbs up it. At first I thought it was too floral and citrus-y, but I'll put a splash of cream or cut it with Wegmans Decaf and it's very drinkable that way.

name: Hibiscus Tea
description: This blend supports the cardiovascular system. Tart, tangy and fruity. Fun, gregarious and creative. Caffeine Free.

rating.description: It's not very good. It tastes like hibiscus. It says it's tart and fruity, and I'd say that's correct. It's tart and fruity. It's not something I'm going to try to get used to.

name: J-Basket Bancha
description: Dry green tea leaves. Kawayanagi Tea.

rating.description: It's good green tea. I like loose leaf tea, I like Japanese green tea, and this is a perfectly acceptable one for an evening drink.

name: Coffee House
description: We infused our House Lager with Wegmans Donut Shop Blend Coffee to give your favorite lager a buzz. Drink Coffee House from morning to night!

rating.description: Very smooth, bordering on sweet, with a lingering coffee taste. This is nice.

name: Bochi Bochi
description: Brewed in the crisp Japanese style with whole Calrose Rice. Very easy-drinking and pleasant on the palate with a mild floral balance from Oregon-grown Tettnang whole-leaf hops. Kanpai!

rating.description: I'm a fan. Rice lagers are underrated, especially brewed Japanese style. This is a good one for those days you really don't want to feel the effects of alcohol at all, but want a nice cold beer that doesn't offend with its weakness and is craft brew quality.

name: Palmera
description: This Colombian offering consists of coffees from several smallholder farmers in the Huila department of southern Colombia. We love how this coffee features so many of the quintessential qualities we enjoy in great Colombian coffees, like a berry acidity, creamy body, and caramel sweetness. Notes: Strawberry, Caramel, Smooth.

rating.description: I give it a thumbs up. It's one of many coffees I've gotten through Trade that are very subtle, very non-offensive, and are good, but not stunningly memorable.

name: Colombia Del Campo
description: Colombian beans, a medium-dark roast, and tasting notes of Marzipan, Chocolate Cherry.

rating.description: I'm a little confused between the vendor's website and Trade's website as to what the tasting notes are supposed to be, but it's a good mellow coffee and I was not sad to drink it.

name: Organic Theo Blend
description: This blend of exceptional coffees from Peru and Honduras features enticing aromas of vanilla bean, black pepper and chocolate. Medium-bodied with herbaceous, dark fruit flavors and a finish of nutmeg and brown sugar. Tastes like dark chocolate, baking spice, dark berries.

rating.description: I don't know if I taste all those flavors mentioned in their description of Theo Blend, but for the kinds of coffees Whole Foods wants to stock these days, I'd say go for this one. There are some other Washington coffees there I would NOT recommend, but I'm a repeat buyer of this one.

name: Sweater Weather
description: We wanted a super cozy coffee awesome enough to cut through the snow and freezing rain of the Pacific Northwest. This Fair Trade Organic sweet pastry of a coffee comes from Chiapas, Mexico. It has been awhile since we’ve had a Mexican coffee and we’re stoked for its return. It brews nicely as a precise pour over. Our recipe calls for 21g semi fine ground coffee, 300g 95C water. We use the ceramic Origami pour over and have achieved great results using the Matt Winton 5 pour recipe but deviating by using a the Origami setup.

rating.description: This is one of my favorite Trailhead coffees currently. I don't taste all the notes they proclaim I will, but I also don't taste sweater, and that's a bonus. It actually is a very nice morning cup of coffee.

name: Decaf Colombian Whole Bean Coffee
description: Decaffeinated light-medium roast coffee with fruity notes, prominent acidity, mild sweetness and floral aroma. 100% Arabica coffee, sourced and roasted with care to deliver a delightful coffee experience in every cup.

rating.description: I don't like it as well as the regular Columbian. I wouldn't drink it without the sugar.

name: Beestly Organic Honey Porter
description: An award-winning, organic, robust American Porter that exudes clover and honey aromas with delicate notes of caramel with a light, roasty finish.

rating.description: I like this better than other Hopworks beer I've tried. I taste the honey. It's a good porter. I won't say "OMG" and rush out to buy it again, but I like it.

name: Thal
description: A unique, floral note of cardamom makes this fruity, balanced coffee really stand out.

rating.description: I didn't necessarily taste all the notes like I thought I should, but it's a nice, neutral, pleasant cup of coffee.

name: Sidamo
description: Sooooo good! Bright with hints of strawberry and graham cracker. Excellent as espresso, French press or drip.

rating.description: It's not a world-beater, but it's a decent cup of coffee.

name: Christmas Ale
description: The chill of winter calls for a beer with extra flavor and strength! An abundance of carefully roasted malts create notes of caramel and chocolate, while Chinook and Mt. Hood hops contribute a spicy quality for balance and a clean finish.

rating.description: It's a Christmas Ale. I like it, and I'll happily drink it, but I don't miss it the entire rest of the year.

name: Folkvangr
description: Dark farmhouse ale fermented with Norwegian kviek yeast. 6.7% ABV

rating.description: It's dark, it's good, it's not bitter. What's not to like?

name: Sicilian Roast The Godfather
description: Our darkest roast, also know as 'The Godfather', is a dream for those who enjoy dark roasted coffee. A heavy-bodied Sicilian roast with sweet bourbon notes and a smooth, smoky finish.

rating.description: I like this one. I'm a fan of dark roasts. Good coffee.

name: Hologram
description: Elevate your coffee experience to a new dimension. Hologram is an extraordinary medium-roast blend that showcases the finest coffees from around the world. Tantalizing notes of ripe fruit and chocolate create a multidimensional flavor experience that's as complex as it is approachable.

rating.description: Hologram may require a different brewing method than I used, but it's slightly bitter. It's certainly not the best Counter Culture coffee I've had. I'm going to give it a thumbs down. This is the first time I've given a thumbs down to a coffee on this podcast.

name: Tantamount Stout
description: This dark, full-bodied stout has complex flavors of dark chocolate and coffee, as well as a smooth molasses like sweetness. Ingredients: Water, Millet, Rice, Buckwheat, Oats, Hops and Yeast.

rating.description: I'm going to give this a thumbs up, and yet it's a little thin and slightly medicinal. It's still better than that Blackbird stout that I really wanted to like. I really like the idea of gluten-free beers.

name: Oktoberfest Märzen
description: As it was forbidden to brew in summer, a stronger beer -- the Märzen -- was brewed earlier in March. It would finally be served at the Oktoberfest, under the "Heaven of Bavaria." We have returned once again to the age-old recipe and recreated that gloriously smooth, honey-coloured piece of history from times gone by. Perfect with: Bavarian sausage salad and all the titbits a true Bavarian would also enjoy: roast chicken, sausages or suckling pig cooked in Wiesn beer.

rating.description: It is malty, it is toasty, and it is crisp. Very happy, this is good.

name: Highbrow Blend
description: REMINDS US OF: Dark chocolate, walnut, cola. BEST AS: Drip or espresso. ROAST LEVEL: Medium

rating.description: Nice and smooth, no bitterness. I definitely smell and taste the nuttiness.

name: OktoBAERfestbier
description: Oktobaerfestbier is a German-style Märzen lager brewed with Czech Saaz and Liberty hops for spicy'n'herbal'n'fruity hop character that lays beautifully over a toasty'n'bready'n'rich malt presence that finishes crispy'n'dry. Drinks best out of your favorite bierstiefel (or boot-shaped glass!). Prost!

rating.description: I enjoy this version of an Oktoberfest beer. They don't tell me on the can what tasting notes to expect, so I believe I can taste crackers. Crackers and ... october... festivals. Anyway, it's good. You'll like it.

name: Oktoberfest
description: Oktoberfest is a Märzen style beer brewed by Opa Opa Brewing Company in Easthampton, MA

rating.description: If I were a beer, this is what I'd be.

name: Piston Pale Ale
description: This latest update in our Pale Ale project explodes onto the senses with exuberant amounts of modern German hop varieties imparting an herbal earthy lemony spiciness.

rating.description: Too hoppy. I haven't really liked any Laurelwood beers except for their Free Range Red Ale. This one is a pale ale and not an IPA, but still it's just too hoppy.

name: Three Philosophers
description: Rich and complex, this tour de force is a glorious blend of elegant Belgian-style quadruple ale and authentic Belgian kriek, its malty depth and gentle sweetness enhanced by sparkling carbonation and a serendipitous touch of cherry. Pouring a mysterious chestnut brown, Three Philosophers is the perfect beer for leisurely sipping and quiet contemplation. The meaning of life? Even if you don't quite get there, this beer is sure to sweeten the journey.

rating.description: I think my tastes have changed because I'm not enjoying this as much as I used to. It tastes too strong.

name: Fall Hornin’ Pumpkin Ale
description: With a brilliant, deep copper hue and creamy beige-colored head, our Fall Hornin' Pumpkin Ale has inviting aromas of caramelized malt and baking bread with highlights of cinnamon, nutmeg, pumpkin and seasonal spices. The pleasantly creamy mouthfeel and silky body embrace the sweet caramel flavors and tang of spices (with just hint of hops) that ends in a smooth, round finish.

rating.description: In general, pumpkin spice anything is overrated, but this is very good for a pumpkin spice. I'm giving it a thumbs up.

name: Hingakawa
description: This coffee is amazing. We are beyond excited to have it in our wheelhouse. Drink it. Love it. Juicy with notes of Papaya and Brown Sugar. Superb as a pour over and a punchy little beast as SO espresso. As espresso, you might utter the following, 'Whoa…wtf…Dang…ok…ok, yeah' in a coming to terms with the amazing taste. Kind of punk rock that way but quite delicious in the end. I put a photo of the grounds in an Origami brewer so you can see the color and richness of this dense little bean.

rating.description: I might have brewed it a tiny bit weak. I don't get the Papaya for sure. The brown sugar I could believe. It's good. It's not a bad coffee, it's just I don't always pick up the flavors they say I should pick up.

name: Oktoberfest Fest Brew
description: Oktoberfest is a brew inspired by traditional Bavarian Festbiers and crafted for celebration every fall. It pours a sunny golden hue with a fluffy foam cap and boasts a clean malt backbone from Vienna and Munich malts. Hallertau Mittelfruh hops add light bitterness to complement the bready aromatics and slightly sweet body. Spirited, yet delicate, and supremely refreshing.

rating.description: Oh, it tastes just like every other Athletic Brewing beer that I've had. In other words, this tastes like a hoppy, non-alcoholic lager or maybe even their IPA, just slightly less hoppy.

name: Cougar Bait
description: Any fisherman worth his salt will tell you - it's all about the bait. Lucky for you, you're holding the good stuff. An American Blonde Ale, clean and crisp, Cougar Bait is sure to help you with your catch, whatever you may be fishing for.

rating.description: It doesn't really say anything about any flavor notes I'm supposed to be looking for, it just says American Blonde Ale.  I don't know enough about the different kinds of beers to really say, but it's good. I like it.

name: Endless Trail
description: Specifically crafted to get you out on the trail. Robust all business sort of coffee. Notes of mulled wine, cinnamon & toasted rice. Very balanced and syrupy that holds its flavors in a thermos rather well. It'll get you to the summit, view or secret spot with ease. May all of our trails be endless.

rating.description: Yeah, I can taste the cinnamon, sure. It's good.

name: Zoigl-Weiss
description: German malts provide the light breadiness while German hops give this beer a light spicy flavoring. The Bavarian Hefeweizen yeasts strain provides the rest: banana ester with a light phenolic clove note. This beer can be paired with nearly any food and is great for drinking on its own as well.

rating.description: This is a good wheat beer. It's not the clearest, there's some cloudiness to it, and I really like it. It's good. The good beer with the s%&+ website.

name: Shotgun Wedding
description: BROWN ALE AGED ON VANILLA BEANS

rating.description: This is a nice dark one. I'm gonna give that the thumbs up! I like it!

name: Wood Chopper
description: This is our take on the classic Belgian-style wit bier. We layered in coriander, Curaçau orange peel, and lime zest to solidify the soft malt base. Easy drinking, spice and citrus. 4.5% ABV

rating.description: The artwork on this can looks like the same style artwork as used for the Portland Century jerseys a few years ago. It's cool. 4.5% ABV for the win! It's a good, easy drinking wheat. This is a thumbs-up. I hope Whole Foods keeps this one in stock. Maybe Little Beast Brewing should sponsor our podcast.

name: Tres Arroyos Mexican Lager
description: This easy-drinking Mexican Cerveza transports you south of the border. Pilsner malt and Saaz hops create a clean, crisp and refreshing lager, while traditional flaked maize adds just a touch of sweetness. Lagered for for up to two months, Tres Arroyos is sure to please the most discerning palate. Salud!

rating.description: This is a good beer with what you would consider summer foods. Very light, very easy to drink with a *slight* bit of zing to it.

name: Peru
description: There is no description provided by the roaster, unfortunately.

rating.description: A really nice locally roasted coffee that was a suprise gift and a wonderful find. Would absolutely buy again.

name: Non-alcoholic
description: The taste of the original in a non-alcoholic brew. Meet Corona Non-alcoholic. It has the same crisp and balanced taste of your favorite Mexican Lager. Add a lime wedge and enjoy anytime.

rating.description: It tastes like a Corona.

name: Pre Pro
description: In the years leading up to Prohibition, there was an explosion of breweries built by German immigrants brewing beers that took the best of the homeland and mixed it with the best of their new country, much like our brewery today. Celebrate our country and it’s orgins with this Pre-Prohibition Pilsner brewed with corn and old school American hops to create a classic American combo.

rating.description: Not as good as the Maifest, but it is good. I would buy it again and I would drink it again. In fact, I AM drinking it again.

name: Back Pedal Brew
description: Roast: Medium, Flavor Profile: Savory Smooth Structured, Origin: Brazil Indonesia.

rating.description: No bitterness, no acidity, but not the smoothest of the smooth. Probably not in my favorites list, but it's a good, solid cup of coffee.

name: Felix Pilsner
description: Latin for lucky, this Bohemian style pilsner lager is named in honor of JP and Amelia’s first child, Felix. This pilsner is smooth and clean with a balanced hop flavor. Brewed with sorghum, brown rice, Belgian-style candi sugar, Czech Saaz hops, Oregon Magnum hops, yeast, and water. Made in the classic Pilsner style, this beer is brewed under strict temperature control and lagered (laid up) for two weeks.

rating.description: This tastes a LOT like the Buoy Czech Pilsner. Very good, not my favorite, but it is one of the better gluten-free beers I've tried.

name: Oregon Sunshine Golden Ale
description: There is no description provided by the brewer, but's locally sourced ingredients engineer to be pest resistant.

rating.description: It's a good ale, slightly darker than some, with a touch of bitterness. I do like it but I won't buy it again on purpose because it's not my favorite ale of all time.

name: Maifest
description: Celebrate the arrival of warmer weather with Maifest. This golden lager, named after the springtime counterpart to Oktoberfest, features Pilsner malt and noble hops for sweet and balanced taste.

rating.description: I'm a fan. Obviously this is a thumbs up for sure.

name: Cream Ale
description: Crisp, clean, classic. Where Ales meet Lagers, a uniquely American brew is born. Our Cream Ale is fresh and inviting, with a restrained use of Willamette hops for a crisp, familiar finish. It's like those days we get here, where impossibly big clouds frame the purest, sunniest sky you can imagine.

rating.description: This is easily my favorite Buoy beer so far. Smooth, flavorful, and light. This is a wonderful summer beer.

name: House Party Pale Ale
description: Fascinatingly fruity but not necessarily hoppy, this unfiltered Pale Ale is bold with notes of passionfruit, rhubarb, and grapefruit.

rating.description: It's not as good as their El Lager Dorado, but I like it. It's not an ale that I'll search for, but it is a smooth drinking beer.

name: Belgian White
description: A wheat beer brewed with Valencia orange peel for a subtle sweetness and bright, citrus aroma. Valencia Orange Peel and Coriander. Garnished with an orange slice to heighten the citrus aroma and taste.

rating.description: It's a Belgian White, but it's really a domestic beer. I like it better than your standard selections of domestic beers.

name: Organic Whole Bean Peruvian Decaf
description: Nutty with a Sweet Finish.

rating.description: Unlike most of my normal go-tos, this is a light roast, and it's pretty good! I had a splash of cream in it, and it's very drinkable.

name: El Lager Dorado
description: El Lager Dorado is brewed with maize and wild agave syrup to create a crisp, refreshing lager with a special zing. ¡Salud!

rating.description: One of the better lagers I've had. A good summer beer. It's light, relatively low alcohol, and very easy drinking.

name: I Believe in Nashville Blonde Ale
description: The I Believe In Nashville Blonde Ale is brewed right here in Nashville. We wouldn’t have it any other way.

rating.description: I think you'd like this. Almost no hop. Very malty. Like Yuengling but without any bitter taste.

name: Czech Pilsner
description: Bright traditional taste. A classic pilsner with roots in the great beer heritage of the Czech Republic. Our Czech-Style Pilsner features Saaz hops supporting layers of rounded malt flavors. Fresh crackers with noble hop bitterness, clean finish.

rating.description: Not the absolute best Pilsner I've ever had, but it's good. I think I'd have it with pizza.

name: Copper Legend
description: Oktoberfest is the world’s most legendary beer festival and it deserves a legendary beer. Copper Legend is the perfect marriage of caramel, sweet toasty malts, and infinite drinkability. Raise one this fest season and Be The Legend!

rating.description: I'm a fan. Obviously this is a thumbs up for sure. Copper Legend is marked by its robust and bready malt character, featuring undertones of caramel sweetness. It's well balanced, with a light hop bitterness that keeps the sweetness in check.

name: Pils
description: Tasting Notes: Fresh flowers, white peppercorn and lightly toasted crackers.

rating.description: I don't know if I would have known this was supposed to taste like peppercorn and crackers if the can didn't say it, but I *can* taste it. I like it. Feels somewhat light and refreshing. Great summer beer.

name: English Breakfast Black Tea
description: A Robust Blend of Black Teas. Steep and enjoy! Allow us to share with you the most natural and authentic tea experience in your cup.

rating.description: A good breakfast tea. I like black teas and I enjoy this one in general. I tend to like breakfast teas. It's very drinkable.

description: Guinness 0 boasts a beautifully smooth taste, perfectly balanced flavor, and unique dark color, similar to Guinness Draught, brewed to be non-alcoholic. The resulting product is a non-alcoholic stout that is unmistakably Guinness, inspired by the same dark, ruby red liquid and creamy head, hints of chocolate and coffee, smoothly balanced with bitter, sweet and roasted notes.

rating.description: Pretty much like a Guinness, just a little flatter.

name: Barista
description: Barista is a Double Coffee Porter, aged on locally roasted coffee beans by our friends at Abracadabra Coffee Company in Woodstock, VT. We age this Robust Porter on more than Two Pounds of Coffee per Barrel for an intense character of freshly brewed Coffee, complimented by malt flavors and aromas of Dark Chocolate, Raisins, Caramel, and Vanilla.

rating.description: It's no mochaccino, and supposedly they still make mochaccino, but it's a distant second, maybe a third even. Oh, it's a good beer!

name: Robust Porter
description: Our Robust Porter is brewed with eight malts to make a roasty brew with coffee and chocolate in the nose, balanced by complex caramel malt flavor and a medium full, malty mouthfeel. One of the five beers we had on draft the day we opened!

rating.description: Slightly bitter, but I like it. I'll drink this again. It's a good porter that's not overly barrel aged or smoky or leathery. It's just a good porter.

name: Special Effects Pils
description: Everybody (well, almost everybody!) loves a pilsner for two main reasons: crisp refreshment, and an easy, approachable style. Our Special Effects Pils delivers on all those beloved pilsner characteristics, just without the buzz, so there’s no distractions to keep you from enjoying this remarkably refreshing brew. Its familiar, easy flavor profile makes it a surefire crowd pleaser, its clean edge makes it the perfect palate cleanser between courses or as a daytime picnic companion, and it’s exactly what you’ll want to reach for for some snappy refreshment at the end of a long day. Special Effects Pilsner invites you to kick back, take a crisp sip, and focus on flavor.

rating.description: I said I was desperate to drink this, but I'm not desperate to drink it and I'm also not desperate to drink it. It's a good non-alcoholic beer, which means it's a bit weak but it's also not bad.

name: River Trip
description: Our yearly homage to summer. A clean and bright cup that perfectly compliments a morning sun peaking over canyon walls. A combination of seasonal, fresh coffees from our longest-standing partners in Guatemala and Africa. Tasting Notes: Orange, Macadamia Nut, and Fudgesicle-like Chocolate.

rating.description: Trippy bag, but good honest flavor that's not THAT out there. I like it. I want it. I'll buy it again.

name: Shepplekofeggan
description: The hard-saying yet easy-drinking Shepplekofeggan was created as an ode to friendship. Pronounced “shêp-ul-kof-again”, it is named after four friends who love their lighter beers; it’s namesakes “Sheets-Epple-Intelkoffer-Duggan” inspired this refreshing Belgian Witbier, which is finished with fresh orange zest and coriander and packed full of citrusy flavor. It just begs for great friends to share it with, and is proof that all Belgian-style beers don’t have to be big in alcohol -- only big in flavor.

rating.description: Good enough for my wife to steal. We like wheats, we like spices, and this is a good example of all of those.

name: Blood Orange
description: Refreshing and hydrating, HOP WTR Blood Orange is packed with Citra, Amarillo, Mosaic and Azacca hops, delivering a bright, citrusy flavor with a strong hint of hops, all with no calories and no sugar.

rating.description: Something you would probably only drink when you're desperate. It's like a club soda with some kind of flavor that is not beer.

name: Classic Belgian Sour Ale
description: Rodenbach Classic sets the bar for Flemish red-brown ales. This ale owes its sweet and sour fruitiness and refreshing taste to the fact that it is partially matured in oak casks.

rating.description: Not excessively sour, and quite drinkable, so we're good!

name: Blueberry Boyfriend
description: Real boyfriends are idiots. Blueberry Boyfriends are always there for you.

rating.description: This is very sour, and I LOVE it. The lemon zest doesn't really show up in the taste profile except to make sure the blueberry is not too sweet. Great stuff.

name: Cafe Carmelita
description: Hands down our #1 coffee, Cafe Carmelita is smooth and delicious. This timeless blend is roasted to bring out notes of cocoa and caramel. Whether you’re making coffee at home or the office, this is one crowd-pleaser.

rating.description: I like it, even though it initally brewed slightly bitter for me. Brew it at 200 degrees like it asks for, and you'll be glad you did.

name: Pineapple IPA
description: We are stoked to offer this tasty IPA where mountain pine aromas collide with the tropics. Flavorful hops blend with a splash of pineapple to create a party in a can.

rating.description: So hoppy. SO. HOPPY. I don't understand the appeal of IPAs. I bought this because somehow while I saw and got excited by the word pineapple, I completely missed the all-caps IPA right below it.

name: Pomegranate
description: Schöfferhofer Pomegranate is the unique combination of sparkling smooth Schöfferhofer unfiltered hefeweizen beer with natural pomegranate flavored drink. Delicious exotic notes of pomegranate meet the crisp, smooth taste of hefeweizen for a uniquely refreshing beer.

rating.description: A solid thumbs-up. Not quite as good as the grapefruit, but very tasty.

name: Yacht Rocket
description: Urban Family Brewing Co. says nothing about their own beer, because their website is one of those MANY, MANY beer websites that doesn't actually feature a list of the beers they sell in stores.

rating.description: Sour, light, and refreshing. I will definitely drink this again.

name: Special Effects Hoppy Amber
description: Brooklyn Special Effects Hoppy Amber tastes just like a regular beer, but therein lies the special effect: it’s not. We use a special fermentation method that develops the flavors, aromas & character of beer with none of the alcohol, and a generous dry hopping resulting in lively hop notes and a clean finish.

rating.description: This tastes probably like what IPA drinkers consider beer. That said, this tastes more like an amber ale with some hoppiness. It's like a watery amber ale. It's pretty weak, but it has some flavor that is not offensive, and I have to say, I drink it when I'm not desperate.

name: Blonde Espresso Roast
description: Experience the lighter side of espresso—a soft, beautifully balanced flavor profile that pairs perfectly with milk (or your favorite nondairy alternative). Made up of select Latin American and East African beans, this blend is carefully roasted to coax out sweet, vibrant notes of candied apple and bittersweet chocolate. The result is smooth, well-rounded and versatile, delicious served hot or over ice.

rating.description: As for the coffee I use for cold brew, it uses a LOT of beans, so I use what ever is on special offer in the supermarket. For my Aeropress and my moka pot I’m rather fond of Starbucks Blonde Espresso beans, but I do also like to mix it up to keep things interesting. I end up going Starbucks, something else, Starbucks, something else, Starbucks…

name: Matcha Toasted Rice
description: A classic blend of genmaicha and matcha teas, Matcha Toasted Rice has a savory, nutty flavor. We blend sencha green tea with toasted rice to make Genmaicha, a traditional Japanese tea. The result is a smooth, rich brew with earthy depth and undertones of brightness.

rating.description: Is it the world's most exquisite green tea? No. Could you get better green tea? Yes. Do I like this? Yes, I do. I will have this tea again. It's so easy to make and quite comforting.

name: Kagoshima Green Tea
description: One of the best Senchas from the Kagoshima area in southern Japan, this brew is light in the cup with a good balance of sweet and bitter flavors.

rating.description: I grew up on Kagoshima green tea, and this is a pretty good one. I might need to experiment with the brewing a bit, but overall, very satisfying.

name: Pineapple, Guava, Passion Radler
description: The most refreshing beer style for fun in the sun. The Radler was invented for crowds of German cyclists and we’re sharing our beer and fruit blends for whatever you’re up to this summer.

rating.description: A rather weak, not so flavorful beer.

name: Melon Cart
description: Tastes like freshly cut melons and the California sun right in your hand. This light, crisp Wheat Ale is bursting with watermelon, honeydew, and cantalope flavors, finishing bright and refreshing.

rating.description: This one is a whopping 4% alcohol. I enjoyed this more than I expected to. Now I think this has more flavor than the Guava Cart.

name: Grapefruit
description: Schöfferhofer Grapefruit is the unique combination of sparkling smooth Schöfferhofer unfiltered wheat beer with natural grapefruit flavoured drink. A refreshing, well-rounded taste with tangy character and hints of sweetness is pleasing to palate.

rating.description: A definite thumbs-up, one of my repeats. It is well-rounded and pleasing, just like they say.

name: Blackbird Stout
description: Our newest year-round release, a long-awaited stout! Blackbird Stout is brewed with malted millet and malted rice for a dark, earthy, roasty flavor. An instant favorite. Brewed with malted millet, malted rice, hops, yeast, and water.

rating.description: Not the best gluten-free beer I've had... It does taste little bitter to me. Wanted to like it but I can't recommend it.

name: Triple Fruited Tripel
description: A fruited feast for the senses. Delightful aromas of ripe peach, creamy mango and juicy orange, with a hint of carbonation to tickle the nose. Three fruits, three times added to a balance blend of citrusy hops makes each sip more refreshing than the last. Well-complimented by a vibrant ginger hue and sitting nicely at 9% ABV, Triple Fruited Tripel makes for an easy drinking ale that's juicy and smooth.

rating.description: A mere 9.0% alcohol. Probably my favorite brewery and a nice strong fruity beer.

name: Nayo Ovalle
description: Look for well-rounded notes of orange, almond butter, and milk chocolate in the cup.

rating.description: Coava is probably my favorite current roaster, and this is another smooth blend. Yes! Recommend!

name: Salted Caramel Porter
description: A lightly-roasted, mahogany-colored, medium-bodied malt that is as smooth as a Marvin Gaye love song. With a sweet, salted-caramel flavor, this special porter is a delicious ale you’ll want to enjoy over and over.

rating.description: This is a great porter. It's only 5.8%, which is great, and it's tasty and smooth. Drink it!

name: Chai Love Spiced Chai Black Tea
description: Spiced Chai black tea, high caffeine.

rating.description: Chai with black tea. Lovely! The cardamom is hitting me hard.

name: S.O. Blend
description: Top quality specialty coffees from East Africa, Central, & South America offer caramel sweetness, chocolate layered with complex fruit notes, and crisp acidity. This tried and true coffee is the kind of cup you want to drink every day. Rich. Chocolatey.

rating.description: Like all Coava coffees, it's smooth and mellow and I love it. Another great one for pour overs.

name: Costa Rica Santa Maria De Dota
description: One of our favorite coffees here at Backporch and a coffee we have been purchasing for about a decade now. This coffee staple at Backporch is sweet, winey, chocolatey, citrusy and delicious. Cupping Notes: Clean Orange Citrus, Milk Chocolate and Winey.

rating.description: I love all the Backporch coffees, and this is no exception. Will drink again.

name: DUNKIN’ BLUEBERRY MATCHA IPA
description: Brand new for 2021, this hazy IPA is inspired by Dunkin’s Blueberry Matcha Latte. Brewed with blueberries, Dunkin’ matcha, and a blend of traditional and modern hops, it’s both tea-like and tropical with bright, juicy notes of mixed berry. Available only in the Dunkin’ Dozen Mix Pack!

rating.description: This is a beer. This may be the only IPA I've ever thought actually tasted good. A seasonal brew from two home teams with blueberries and matcha.

name: Marryin' Berries
description: Made for the assistant brewer's wedding this kettle sour is made with white wheat, flaked oats, marrionberries, raspberries, and mosaic.

rating.description: SOUR! Berries! Ex Novo! What's not to love? (Answer: their crappy website) Their beer is amazing though.

name: Backporch Blend
description: This is a favored staple here at Backporch. Syrupy and sweet, with hints of dark chocolate, cherries, cane sugar and caramel.

rating.description: Very smooth and nice. Easy to brew, easy to drink.

name: The Darkness
description: The Darkness is bigger and bolder than anything you've had before. It celebrates a heavy, syrupy body, making it the perfect choice for a hard-hitting espresso with a full flavour of vanilla, almond and dark chocolate.

rating.description: I was drawn in by the package. I taste the richness, but calling it chocolatey is a stretch. It is bitter but it is smooth. A bit of a slap in your face kind of coffee, which is kind of what I need in the morning. Not too bad in all.

name: French Roast Dark
description: Intense and smoky, the pure, explosive flavor of French Roast is as dark as our dark roasts get.

rating.description: A dark french roast best made as an espresso.

name: Silver Imperial
description: La cerveza de los costarricenses desde 1924

rating.description: All Imperial beers are in the 4% ABV range.

name: Third Bird Oatmeal Stout
description: Smooth and soft, with subtle notes of coffee and chocolate, this oatmeal stout is a fine choice for any time of day, whether you're an early bird or a night owl. 6.0% ABV

rating.description: A really nice smooth Oatmeal Stout that I will absolutely buy again.

name: Guava Cart
description: A light & refreshing wheat ale made with real guava.

rating.description: Not as sweet as Mango Cart, but higher alcohol. It has a nice guava flavor and the slightest hint of bitterness at the very end. Not unpleasant like most IPAs though.

name: Peanut Butter Milk Stout
description: Troy came up with the idea of combining the flavor of peanut butter with our milk stout and he nailed it. Don’t let the dark color fool you, this beer is delightfully easy to drink with cascading aromas of roasted peanuts, dark chocolate and coffee. Good times to you my friend, and welcome to the beaver family!

rating.description: This is the best peanut butter milk stout I've found. Very slightly bitter, but it is a favorite and I have purchased it multiple times. It does not make me belch, and I'm not a beaver, even though I do live in the Pacific Northwest.

name: Wonderland Winter Blend
description: The perfect cozy blend for misty mornings. Medium roast, wonderfully balanced with festive tasting notes of baking spice, brown sugar and toasted nuts.

rating.description: Not necessarily in my top five of coffees, but I will and did buy this again. It's easy to make a smooth cup of coffee with this roast, and it's a nice drinking morning coffee.

name: Distant Horizon Whole Bean Coffee
description: Bold with notes of dark chocolate. Blend of beans from Colombia, Brazil, Ethiopia and Nicaragua. From Crop to Cup: Sourced and Roasted with Care.

rating.description: I like it a lot. I had 3 cups in one day, and I didn't put any cream in, which I normally do with coffee.

name: San Marcos Honduras
description: Look for a sweet and balanced profile with notes of stewed pear, brown sugar, and baker's chocolate in the cup.

rating.description: This one grew on me. It's nice and mellow, mellower than I expected, but a very nice one.

name: Slow Motion
description: For Slow Motion, we start by selecting the same high-quality coffees that appear in our other offerings and gently decaffeinate them in small batches using organic processing. Tasting notes: Smooth molasses and cocoa.

rating.description: Tasty, a tiny bit more acidic than I like, but definitely a drinkable coffee that I will buy again.

name: Sunbreak Morning Blend
description: With notes of chocolate and nuts, this is an ideal coffee when you need to satisfy a wide range of coffee drinkers. Family gathering with some crusty bugger demanding darkness and your fancy people from PDX who will not tolerate bitterness except well… never mind.

rating.description: I do love me a good Trailhead, and this is a nice mellow one.

name: Gingerbread Flavored Tea
description: Limited Edition. Our Food You Feel Good About yellow banner is your shortcut to great-tasting products with no artificial colors, flavors or preservatives.

rating.description: A black tea with caramel notes. It has a very smooth mouth feel to it.

name: Sleigh'r Winter Ale
description: A limited release. Roasty, Toffee, Malty.

rating.description: Winter ales tend to be ever so slightly bitter, and this one fits that mold, but it's pretty good. I do taste the roasty, toffee, malty flavor they claim. I wouldn't fight an angry mob for it, but it is worth drinking.

name: Study Hall
description: Study Hall is a classic Amber ale conditioned on Maple Coffee roasted by Speeder & Earls. Flavors and aromas of Maple candy, French Roast Cold Brew, Caramel, Toffee, and Maple frosted Coffee Cake.

rating.description: Lighter than the Burlington Beer Co. Moccacino, but very, very good.

name: Breakfast Blend
description: Notes of sweet orange and brown sugar mingle in our lightest medium roast coffee.

rating.description: It’s more about the French Press and less about the coffee.

name: Red
description: Deep dark red colour, with a light pink, compact and lacing head. Soft fruity aroma, with hints of almond and mildly sour cherries. Sweet and fruity, with a nice balance between sweet and sour. An excellent dessert beer.

rating.description: A little too sweet, a little too much like drinking cherry syrup

name: White
description: The Original Belgian Wheat Beer. Almost 600 years ago in the Belgian village of Hoegaarden, a band of monks experimented by adding oddball botanicals from halfway around the world to their traditional wheat beer. Our recipe, inspired by their creation, is a beer with a refreshing flavor and captivating aroma, unlike any in the world. Let the refreshing citrus and earthy coriander alleviate the stresses of modern living and whisk you to another place entirely. You might call it divine inspiration... we call it Hoegaarden.

rating.description: It’s a touch weak and a lot wheat.

name: Santa's Private Reserve Honey Mama's
description: Santa has always been convinced that all great confections come from the North Pole, so we reached out to our friends at Honey Mama’s to help us show him otherwise. The Honey Mama’s crew whipped up some of their favorite tasty treats and we sent them up to Santa in a care package. It’s safe to say he feels a bit differently now, for mere minutes after receiving the delivery Santa was on the phone with us gushing about the delicious goodies, begging us to recreate this in his annual Private Reserve. Per his request. we teamed up with Honey Mama’s to create this tahini, tangerine and chocolate flavored stout. Santa is sure to love it. and so are you.

rating.description: Quite good, much better than last year's Santa's Private Reserve. I enjoy it even though I probably won't buy it again.

name: Festivale
description: It’s raining outside, the fireplace is lit, and you’ve just finished the book you’ve been reading for awhile. A family member comes in and asks if you want a Festivale. Could you really say no? Festivale is a classic TG rendition of a Winter Warmer. Brewed to be fairly dry, yet highly drinkable. With a complex malt and hop profile and a full, rounded, deep ruby colored body- Festivale is a winter favorite that rings true to a wide variety of beer drinkers.

rating.description: It's a good festive ale. Festivale!! I actually like this one, but it's not one I see myself drinking a lot of. Thumbs up, but I won't actively seek it out again.

name: Oktoberfest
description: Dedicating the world’s biggest public festival to beer might seem silly to some, but we Germans are very serious about that – as serious as we are about our limited Warsteiner Oktoberfest Special Edition. This beer is brewed with hand-selected hops, Munich-type spring barley malt and extra-soft brewing water from the Arnsberg forest nature park. Its well-balanced taste will make you feel like you are part of the Oktoberfest, wherever you are.

rating.description: It’s like if a light beer married a German. It wasn’t that great, but not that bad either. Not my first go-to Oktoberfest, but I would drink it even if not desperate.

name: BeachLife POG Pale Ale
description: Beach Life P.O.G Pale Ale is a tropical twist on a classic Pale Ale. Brewed with Amarillo, Cascade, and Idaho 7 hops, these fruit-forward aroma hops, and a moderate dose of P.O.G. “Passionfruit, Orange, and Guava” lend to this very drinkable fruit-forward P.O.G. Pale Ale! The first sip will have you living your beach life and take you to the islands with your toes in the sand.

rating.description: When I saw the can, I had mixed feelings, just like the mix of fruit inside this beer. But I like it! It's good! I'll drink more!

name: Single Track
description: Single Track is our single origin rotating espresso at Backporch. For this Single Track we chose a coffee from Antigua Guatemala under the name of Hunapu. Coffees from Antigua have depth and sweetness going for them, as well as some nice fruited notes. We found this coffee to have notes of: dried fig, cacao nibs and molasses. This coffee is suitable for both espresso and filter.

rating.description: For some reaon I was pessimistic about this becuase I bought it when Whole Foods was out of Trailhead. But I really, really like it! It's smooth and mellow and it's very easy to brew without acidity or overly strong flavor. Do recommend.

name: Subtle Beauty
description: Most high end coffees are like a musical soloist with other musicians in the background where the soloist is the important part. This coffee breaks from that formula where there’s no stand out berry note or chocolate note or aroma of Jasmine. Instead it’s just a lovely balanced cup with autumnal mojo happening. We’re getting aroma notes of: Date, Pecan Roll and Cinnamon Toast. In the cup, we’re tasting Apricot, Pie Crust and Brown Sugar. This coffee is worthy of precise brewing and experimentation. Pay special attention to how this coffee cools as the flavors shift delightfully.

rating.description: Trailhead is one of my favorite local roasters, and this is a very nice mellow roast. I love the lighter brown, non-greasy beans, and this has those plus nice easy flavor.

name: Decaf Espresso Whole Bean Roast
description: Bold, decaffeinated dark roast coffee that is smooth with notes of dark chocolate, cocoa and spice. 100% Arabica coffee, sourced and roasted with care to deliver a delightful coffee experience in every cup. Perfect for espresso shot and espresso based drinks.Our Food You Feel Good About yellow banner is your shortcut to great-tasting products with no artificial colors, flavors or preservatives.

rating.description: This is the best store brand decaf coffee I have had the pleasure of sipping. I only wish they sold it in 5 pound bags.

name: Hell or High Watermelon
description: Hell or High Watermelon Wheat is our summer seasonal beer available from April through September in six pack cans and on draft. We start by brewing a classic American wheat beer, then add fresh melons for a straw-colored, delicious beer with a kiss of watermelon aroma and flavor.

rating.description: A  crisp, refreshing wheat beer infused with watermelon.
I wish it had more watermelon flavor, but it is a nice light wheat beer that's very pleasant.

name: Green State Lager
description: A crisp, easy drinking Pilsner beer. Noble hops in perfect balance with only the finest Pilsner malt provide a clean and satisfying brew that is as welcoming as the Green State itself.

rating.description: After you drink all of this beer, you can fly because you experience zero gravity.

name: Walk the Lime
description: Made with Tennessee wheat. This crisp, tropical and refreshing ale is bursting with fresh lime aromas and flavors of zested citrus and bitter peel, mixing perfectly with a clean wheat-driven finish.

rating.description: A very fun summer ale. If you've ever had a Bud Light lime and wished it was good, this is it! A very tasty refreshing wheat ale.

name: Olallie Ale
description: You can if it’s your destiny, and this beer was destined to be canned. Brewed with blackberries, rosehips and Crystal hops, Olallie was designed from the ground up to be our first canned beer. This crisp, dry, well-balanced, refreshing ale is enjoyable any time of the year. Fun Fact: Olallie is Chinook Jargon for berry.

rating.description: A gluten-free blackberry and rosehip ale. A very fruity drink. I do like these. It's very good.

name: Thresh
description: To allow for this special grain to shine, we brewed a Pale Lager with just a touch of modern flair, achieved with a very subtle dry-hop of Motueka. The gentle hop addition offers a fleeting highlight of key lime and zested citrus, with some floral undertones adding complexity.

rating.description: Pretty good. Not super hoppy, not super bitter, and it is a lager.

name: The Most Interesting Lager In The World
description: Crisp and refreshing, brewed with Saaz hops, Vienna and Pilsner malts, and a hint of flaked corn.

rating.description: A very good Mexican lager that's great with anything.

name: The Rose
description: Our best seller! A rich, golden color with the spicy aroma of clove and candy banana. The Belgian yeast shines bright on the palate, light and silky, with a clean, slightly drying bitter finish. Pairs well with afternoons on the lake; spring fare, white fish and fruit.

rating.description: Created, not made. My wife's go-to beer.

name: Lights Out Stout
description: Our ode to starry, starry nights. Hints of vanilla, coffee & nutty flavors with a creamy finish.

rating.description: A 7.7% alcohol. I like this. Notes of coffee, chocolate, and vanilla, and I'm like this sounds good, but it was the 30 IBUs that sold me.
A nice dark one that I enjoyed very much. Don't let the hops graphic on the can fool you, it's not too hoppy at all.

name: Oat Soda
description: Bohemian-Style Pilsner brewed with malted and flaked oats and our favorite German pilsner malt along with Czech Saaz Hops. The oats add body and allow us to bring the abv down to supremely crushable levels while the Czech Saaz hops build in the right amount of bitterness and spice to keep it complex and oh so satisfying! Na zdravi!

rating.description: This is ok. It's not the worst beer I've ever had. It's definitely a light beer. I might run 5k out of my way for this beer but not 50k.
Have you ever had a pilsner that was better than just ok? I think that Pilsners are a nice beer for a pizza, but not a beer you would just grab.

name: Run Wild IPA
description: Run Wild is the ultimate sessionable IPA for craft beer lovers. Brewed with a blend of five Northwest hops, it has an approachable bitterness to balance the specialty malt body. Always refreshing and only 65 calories.

rating.description: Dear God. Why??? Tastes like desperate regret. This thing makes me want to spit it out, like poison.

name: Puff Puff Passionfruit Sour
description: Tart, tropical fruit, & juicy hops. Brewed with Mosaic and Simcoe hops, and fermented with passion fruit.

rating.description: OMG is it ever sour, but VERY good.

name: Weizen-Radler
description: This mix is in a class of its own – combining the great taste of Paulaner Hefe-Weizen with natural effervescent lemonade in a non-alcoholic alternative for refreshingly fruity yet malty taste. The citrus notes of lime, orange, and lemon match the wheat beer perfectly and provide a uniquely balanced taste experience.

rating.description: A German non-alcoholic beer. Tastes way more than twice as good as the Run Wild IPA. Tastes like drinking a soda or a lemonade.

name: Big Wave Golden Ale
description: Paddle into easy-drinking, island refreshment with Big Wave. So smooth, it’s like catching the crest of a breaking wave at Oahu’s Makaha Beach and gliding all the way into the sandy shore. Paradise is just a sip away, so bring your ohana along for the ride. One life, right?

rating.description: A light ale that tastes like summer and reinforces my friendly feelings towards Kona Brewing.

name: Salvator
description: Paulaner’s brewing history begins with this beer. It was the Paulaner monks who invented this unfiltered bottom-fermented double bock. This beer has been brewed for over 375 years – always adhering to the original recipe, with only a few refinements over the years.

rating.description: Made in Munich by Monks. I'm just trying to think when was the last time I had a beer from Munich that I did not like, and I can't think of any. This one is good!

name: Catamount Porter
description: Our modern revival of the Vermont classic, Catamount Porter boasts a robust smooth character and a roasty-sweet aroma with notes of dark coffee.

rating.description: A nice porter continued under the Catamount label after Catamount Brewery was acquired by Harpoon Brewery.

name: Milagro Oscuro
description: Nothing, because we don't even have our individual beers listed on our website. 🤷

rating.description: Apparently a limited release, it's a nice dark beer that Ex Novo calls a Mexican style lager.

name: Kona Classic Pipeline
description: We say nothing, because this beer isn't listed on our website anymore. 🤷

rating.description: A very nice coffee porter that's dark enough but still easy to drink. No overpowering porter taste.

name: Son of Juice IPA
description: Bursting with notes of tropical fruit, Son of Juice features loads of Mosaic, Mosaic Cryo, Simcoe, Simcoe Cryo, and Nugget hops. Pilsner malt and oats lend to a soft body and some haze, making for a juicy, low-bitterness IPA.

rating.description: It's an IPA. I was going to say I don't hate it, but then the aftertaste kicked in.

name: Golden Monkey
description: Named in part from the golden tips, our Golden Monkey black tea hails from Fujian Province in China where it is traditionally crafted using sun withering, rolling, fermentation, and drying. The tea is strong bodied, with hints of cocoa, malt, and caramel.

rating.description: I love black tea and Chinese teas in general, and this has a nice strong flavor that I really enjoy. I imagine this would be amazing on a cold, rainy night.

name: Tennessee Sipper Golden Light Ale
description: A back to basics beer; smooth and easy-drinking one. Light-bodied, slightly sweet on the backend, and creamy, this beer is an all day crusher.

rating.description: A lighter ale.

name: Mocaccino
description: Mocaccino is a Blond Stout brewed with Coffee, Chocolate, Vanilla, and Milk Sugar. This ale creates a juxtaposition of flavors to appearance. What looks like a light colored pale ale, is actually a beer rich with flavors and aromas of Espresso, Melted Chocolate Bars, and Vanilla Frosting.

rating.description: A blond milk stout with chocolate, coffee, vanilla, and milk sugar. This may very well be my favorite beer.

name: Milk Stout Nitro
description: Experience America’s Stout. Milk Stout Nitro is a full sensory experience. Gaze at the mesmerizing cascade of all those tiny Nitro bubbles. Breathe in the aromas of roasted coffee, milk chocolate, brown sugar and vanilla cream. Savor the super smooth Nitro sensation. And, smile as the perfectly pillowy head coats your upper lip. This portable draft beer experience is Good to Go straight from the can or served Like a Pro in a glass. From the bottle, Pour Hard to release the Nitro magic inside.

rating.description: I can taste the milk in this. Very smooth.

name: Santa's Private Reserve 2021
description: Santa has always been convinced that all great confections come from the North Pole, so we reached out to our friends at Honey Mama’s to help us show him otherwise. The Honey Mama’s crew whipped up some of their favorite tasty treats and we sent them up to Santa in a care package. It’s safe to say he feels a bit differently now, for mere minutes after receiving the delivery Santa was on the phone with us gushing about the delicious goodies, begging us to recreate this in his annual Private Reserve. Per his request. we teamed up with Honey Mama’s to create this tahini, tangerine and chocolate flavored stout. Santa is sure to love it. and so are you.

rating.description: The fact that it was aged on rum barrel chips is apparent when you drink it, and I don't think that's necessarily a good thing.

name: Everything Nice
description: Lightly dusted with spices of the season, Everything Nice is a warming, wintry Belgian-style blonde ale. This supremely cozy confection pairs perfectly with any traditional holiday treat. Note the flavors of cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves, and white pepper as you sip next to the fireplace. We hope this fresh-baked offering brings warmth and light to you and yours.

rating.description: I am in love. This smells like an amazing Indian curry, tastes like a strong belgian ale, and it finishes like gingerbread.

name: Hefeweizen
description: We'll never tell you what we say about this beer, because it's not currently on our website!

rating.description: A good beer for a sunny, summer day.

name: Jam Sesh
description: You'll just have to guess! Why? Currently not on our website!

rating.description: This is a very good one. A blond ale with strawberries.

name: Vanilla Porter
description: Aromas of vanilla and toasted grain set the stage for mellow flavors of vanilla and dark roasted malts in this popular porter. Don't let its deep mahogany color fool you, this brew is packed with flavor, yet as smooth as they come.

rating.description: A good - not too bitter - porter for a cold day.

name: Otis Oatmeal Stout
description: With a simple call, Oatis will come running, whenever you’re in need of a dependable sidekick by your side. Savor its rich, chocolate, and roasty notes and let it warm your soul. Chocolate. Roasty. Rich.

rating.description: A nice smooth oatmeal stout. In my opinion, the best beer Ninkasi offers.

name: Cactus Wins The Lottery
description: We were about forty miles from Corrales when the Berliner Weisse began to take hold. We can’t stop here, this is Prickly Pear Country.

rating.description: A nice sour, light beer that is very appropriate for summer or anytime you want to pretend it's summer.

name: Mango Cart
description: First in a series inspired by the iconic fruit cart vendors of Los Angeles. A light Wheat Ale bursting with lots of fresh mango flavor and aroma, finishing crisp and refreshing.

rating.description: Good enough that I looked it up in the local store and bought a 15-pack.

name: Newport Daze
description: The morning after a long night, we like to hit the beach for some R&R. Newport Daze Hazy Pale Ale is the perfect day sipper for such an occasion. It’s an easy, mellow brew to get you through. This hazy pale gives off aromas of pineapple & stone fruit, features tangerine & peach flavors, and finishes off slightly sweet and very smooth.

rating.description: More tropical, more citrusy. I can taste a little bit of the hops. Not my favorite Rogue beer.

name: Project Pilsner Crystal
description: Our beer is great, but our website isn't. You'll never find any information about this beer there or anywhere else.

rating.description: I like it. I won't fight an angry mob for it, but it's very smooth and easy to drink.

name: Apricot Wheat
description: Our smooth wheat beer is light in color and body…perfect for those looking for a lighter taste. The combination of wheat and barley gives Apricot Wheat a different malt character than our other ales. The hint of apricot gives this beer a pleasant nose and fruity finish.

rating.description: Less sweet than the mango cart, but it's a very good lighter wheat. Tastes much more like apricot than wet dog, and that is a good thing.

name: Vanishing Point Pale Ale
description: For our take on the classic American pale ale, we decided to throw inhibition to the wind and jump in with both feet. With several types of artisan gluten-free millet & rice malts, and four varieties of Washington-grown hops, one sip will make your preconceptions about gluten-free beer Vanish into the great beyond! A balanced beer with malt flavors of caramel and biscuit with classic American hop flavors of stone fruit and citrus.

rating.description: A little hoppy. Not a repeater for me.

name: Honey Kolsch
description: Brewed with wildflower honey, this Kolsch-style ale has layers of subtle floral notes accented by the honey’s natural sweetness that create a refreshing balance with the hops and malts. Honey Kolsch is our liquid ode to bees for all the wonderful work they do to keep the cycle of life turning.

rating.description: A nice light summery beer that's popular with the whole family (but maybe keep it away from the kids).

name: Summer Love Golden Ale
description: In the late 2000’s we created a beer to celebrate all the best of summer - baseball, beach days, and barbecues. Today, that beer has grown into the most iconic seasonal beer ever and the official craft beer of summer - Summer Love. Summer Love is a refreshing Golden Ale that delivers big flavor through its fine balance of clean pilsner malts and citrusy, earthy Simcoe and Tettnang hops.

rating.description: It is good. Love at first sip.

name: Three Philosophers Double Chocolate
description: It’s been said that chocolate is happiness you can eat. Likewise, we contend that Three Philosophers, our Belgian-style quadruple, is wisdom you can drink. Married together, we present a beer for mind and soul; a deeply-considered chocolate philosophy. For this project, we partnered with the artisans at Taza Chocolate, who shared their cocoa and their expertise in pursuit of sweet perfection. Swirl, sip, and melt away… This heavenly confection pours a deep caramel in color with mahogany flecks, topped by a foamy tan head. Semi-sweet cocoa and subtle vanilla prevail in the aroma. The mouthfeel is textured and full-bodied, with caramel, toffee and dark fruit wrapped in the embrace of rich, decadent Taza chocolate, culminating in a refreshingly smooth, lingering finish.

rating.description: Best drunk at around 50F. One of my favorite beers of all time. It's also a commitment because it's a 9% ABV beer.

name: Fivepine Chocolate Porter
description: A robust Porter that features two pounds per barrel of the finest Belgian dark chocolate, creating a slightly roasty pint with underlying chocolate sweetness.

rating.description: One of my favorite chocolate beers. Someone once asked me if it wasn't too chocolatey, to which I replied, "You understand that I'm drinking this by choice, right?".
